title: From assigned probability to perplexity
description: A quick reference for the probability, negative-log, and evaluation terms used here.

terms.definition: The probability a model gives to the observed target under its current context.
The negative natural logarithm of an event's probability; rarer events have greater surprise.
The product of conditional probabilities assigned to every observed target in a sequence.
The sum of negative log probabilities for the observed target events.
Total negative log-likelihood divided by the number of evaluated target tokens.
Dividing total surprise by target count so differently sized samples remain comparable.
The information unit produced when negative log-likelihood uses the natural logarithm.
The exponential of mean NLL, expressed as an equivalent constant prediction difficulty.
Mean NLL interpreted against the empirical distribution of the observed target tokens.
The highest-probability choice, which does not reveal probability assigned to another observed target.
